passage.title: Cambiar dólares en el mostrador
target: Daniel: Buenas tardes. Quisiera cambiar doscientos dólares a euros.
Marta: Claro. El tipo de cambio hoy es de 0,92 euros por dólar, y la comisión es fija.
Daniel: ¿Cuánto recibo en euros, neto, después de la comisión?
Marta: Son 184 euros, menos la comisión de 5 euros. Recibe 179 euros netos.
Daniel: Perfecto. ¿Me puede dar dos billetes de cincuenta?
Marta: Sí. Firme aquí, por favor, y le cuento los billetes.
Daniel: Gracias. Quiero revisar el recibo antes de irme.
Marta: Todo está correcto. Que tenga buen viaje.
native: Daniel: Good afternoon. I would like to exchange two hundred dollars into euros.
Marta: Of course. The exchange rate today is 0.92 euros per dollar, and the fee is fixed.
Daniel: How much do I receive in euros, net, after the fee?
Marta: It is 184 euros, minus the 5-euro fee. You receive 179 euros net.
Daniel: Perfect. Can you give me two fifty-euro notes?
Marta: Yes. Sign here, please, and I will count the notes for you.
Daniel: Thank you. I want to check the receipt before I leave.
Marta: Everything is correct. Have a good trip.

words.note: The number of one currency given for another. Read it with the currency pair stated.
An amount charged for the service of exchanging money.
The amount that remains after fees or deductions have been taken away.
The currency of the United States and several other countries.
A paper note of money. The plural is billetes.
A written proof of the exchange, which you should check before you leave.
The currency used by many European countries. The plural is euros.
A shop or counter where you exchange one currency for another.
Does not change with the amount. Here it refers to a set fee.

words.es: Quisiera cambiar doscientos dólares a euros.
words.en: I would like to exchange two hundred dollars into euros.
words.note: A polite way to state the currency and amount at the start of an exchange.

words.en: How much do I receive in euros, net?
words.note: Asks for the final amount after all fees are taken away.
The formal command the clerk uses to ask for a signature.

words.es: Quiero revisar el recibo antes de irme.
words.en: I want to check the receipt before I leave.
words.note: Says you will verify the document before walking away.
A common closing wish from staff.

example.target: Cambio dólares por euros.
example.native: I exchange dollars for euros.

verbs.note: Cambiar dólares por euros and cambiar dólares a euros both name the currency you receive after por or a.

example.target: Recibe 179 euros netos.
example.native: You receive 179 net euros.

verbs.note: Recibir is regular. Recibe serves for él, ella and usted, so recibe 179 euros can mean you receive.

example.target: Firme el recibo, por favor.
example.native: Please sign the receipt.

verbs.note: Firmar is regular; the usted command firme is used by staff.

passage.title: Tipos de cambio en el tablero
target: Lucía: Perdone, ¿a cuánto está el dólar hoy?
Empleado: En el tablero, la compra es 0,92 euros por dólar: es lo que le pagamos si usted nos vende dólares.
Lucía: ¿Y si yo compro dólares?
Empleado: Entonces se aplica la venta. Si usted compra dólares, paga 0,95 euros por dólar.
Lucía: Entonces, la comisión, ¿está incluida en ese precio?
Empleado: No. La comisión es aparte y son 2 euros por operación.
Lucía: Entonces el precio final tiene que incluir los 2 euros.
Empleado: Exacto. Puede confirmar la cifra en la pantalla antes de pagar.
native: Lucía: Excuse me, what is the dollar rate today?
Clerk: On the board, the buy rate is 0.92 euros per dollar: that is what we pay you if you sell us dollars.
Lucía: And if I buy dollars?
Clerk: Then the sell rate applies. If you buy dollars, you pay 0.95 euros per dollar.
Lucía: So, is the fee included in that price?
Clerk: No. The fee is separate and it is 2 euros per transaction.
Lucía: So the final price has to include the 2 euros.
Clerk: Exactly. You can confirm the figure on the screen before you pay.

words.note: The price of one currency in another. Always check the direction of the quote.
On a rate board, the buy rate: what the bank pays when it buys the currency from you.
On a rate board, the sell rate: what the bank charges when it sells the currency to you.
The display that shows the rate, the fee and the final amount.
One exchange of money, usually with its own fee.
An extra amount charged for the exchange service.
A currency used in several countries.
A man who works at a bank or service counter. The feminine form is empleada.
A number that represents an amount on a board or receipt.

words.en: What is the dollar rate today?
words.note: A natural question for the current price of a currency.

words.es: Si usted compra dólares, paga 0,95 euros por dólar.
words.en: If you buy dollars, you pay 0.95 euros per dollar.
words.note: Explains the rate that applies to a buyer.

words.es: ¿La comisión está incluida en ese precio?
words.en: Is the fee included in that price?
words.note: Confirms whether the amount shown is final.

words.en: It has to include the 2 euros.
words.note: A reminder that a fixed charge must be added to the total.

words.es: Puede confirmar la cifra en la pantalla.
words.en: You can confirm the figure on the screen.
words.note: A clerk's invitation to check the amount before you accept.

example.target: Compro dólares en el banco.
example.native: I buy dollars at the bank.

verbs.note: Comprar is regular and takes the currency as its direct object.

example.target: Vendo cien dólares a 0,92 euros por dólar.
example.native: I sell one hundred dollars at 0.92 euros per dollar.

verbs.note: Vender is regular. A board shows the bank's view: its compra rate is what you get when you sell.

example.target: Confirmo el total en la pantalla.
example.native: I confirm the total on the screen.

verbs.note: Confirmar is regular and often used before a payment is authorized.

passage.title: Dos ofertas para cambiar dólares
target: Rafael: Tengo dos ofertas para cambiar doscientos dólares.
Empleada: La oferta A tiene un tipo de 0,92 y una comisión de 5 euros.
Rafael: ¿Y la oferta B?
Empleada: La oferta B tiene un tipo de 0,90 y no cobra comisión.
Rafael: Entonces con la A recibo 179 euros, y con la B recibo 180.
Empleada: Exacto. La oferta B da un resultado más alto.
Rafael: Entonces la B es mejor que la A, aunque el tipo es menor.
Empleada: Sí, la comisión pesa más que la diferencia del tipo.
Rafael: Perfecto. Quiero cambiar con la oferta B, por favor.
native: Rafael: I have two offers to exchange two hundred dollars.
Clerk: Offer A has a rate of 0.92 and a fee of 5 euros.
Rafael: And offer B?
Clerk: Offer B has a rate of 0.90 and charges no fee.
Rafael: So with A I receive 179 euros, and with B I receive 180.
Clerk: Exactly. Offer B gives a higher result.
Rafael: So B is better than A, even though the rate is lower.
Clerk: Yes, the fee weighs more than the difference in the rate.
Rafael: Perfect. I want to exchange with offer B, please.

words.note: A proposal for an exchange or price, with stated terms.
Setting two amounts side by side to see which is larger.
The final amount after the rate and fee have been applied.
A charge added to an exchange; some offers list none.
A short word for the exchange rate in everyday talk.
The gap between two amounts or two rates.
An offer that does not charge a separate service fee.
The last amount after all adjustments have been made.
Less than the other amount or rate.

words.es: La oferta B es mejor que la oferta A.
words.en: Offer B is better than offer A.
words.note: Compares two offers to conclude which one suits you.

words.es: Con la oferta A recibo menos que con la B.
words.en: With offer A I receive less than with B.
words.note: Compares the final amount received under two options.

words.es: La comisión pesa más que la diferencia del tipo.
words.en: The fee outweighs the difference in the rate.
words.note: A clear explanation of why a small rate difference can lose value.

words.es: Quiero cambiar con la oferta B, por favor.
words.en: I want to exchange with offer B, please.
words.note: Confirms your decision in a polite request.

words.es: Tengo dos ofertas para cambiar doscientos dólares.
words.en: I have two offers to exchange two hundred dollars.
words.note: States the starting point for a comparison.

example.target: Comparo las dos ofertas antes de decidir.
example.native: I compare the two offers before deciding.

verbs.note: Comparar is regular. Use con when you set one option beside another.

example.target: La oferta B no cobra comisión.
example.native: Offer B does not charge a fee.

verbs.note: Cobrar takes a fee or price as its direct object.

example.target: Decido quedarme con la oferta B.
example.native: I decide to go with offer B.

verbs.note: Decidir is regular and is often followed by an infinitive.

example.target: La comisión pesa más de lo que parece.
example.native: The fee matters more than it seems.

verbs.note: Pesar literally means to weigh; pesar más que means to outweigh or count for more.

passage.title: Retirar dinero en el cajero
target: Viajero: Perdone, ¿me cobran comisión por retirar efectivo aquí?
Empleado: Sí, el banco cobra tres euros por cada retiro fuera de la red.
Viajero: ¿Y la pantalla me pregunta si quiero convertir en euros o en dólares?
Empleado: Sí. Si elige la moneda local, el cajero no hace la conversión; la hace su banco.
Viajero: Quiero retirar cien euros, pero cuesta más si elijo dólares, ¿verdad?
Empleado: Normalmente sí. La opción en dólares usa el tipo del cajero, que incluye un recargo.
Viajero: Entonces elijo euros y pido el recibo con la comisión visible.
Empleado: Muy bien. El cajero se lo imprime al final.
native: Traveler: Excuse me, do they charge me a fee for withdrawing cash here?
Staff member: Yes, the bank charges three euros for each withdrawal outside its network.
Traveler: And does the screen ask me whether I want to convert into euros or dollars?
Staff member: Yes. If you choose the local currency, the ATM does not do the conversion; your bank does.
Traveler: I want to withdraw one hundred euros, but it costs more if I choose dollars, right?
Staff member: Usually, yes. The dollar option uses the ATM's rate, which includes a surcharge.
Traveler: Then I choose euros and ask for the receipt with the fee visible.
Staff member: Very well. The ATM will print it for you at the end.

words.note: Taking money out of an account or an ATM.
A machine that gives cash from a bank account. Often shortened to cajero.
A charge for a service such as a withdrawal.
An extra amount added to a price, here built into the rate of the home-currency option.
Changing an amount from one currency into another, often done by a machine.
One act of taking money out of an account.
The group of ATMs or branches that a bank uses without an extra charge.
The currency used in the place you are visiting.
A printed proof of the transaction, showing the fee.
One choice that the machine or staff offers you.

words.es: ¿Me cobran comisión por retirar efectivo aquí?
words.en: Do they charge me a fee for withdrawing cash here?
words.note: Asks about fees before you make the withdrawal.

words.es: Si elige la moneda local, el cajero no hace la conversión.
words.en: If you choose the local currency, the ATM does not do the conversion.
words.note: Explains the cheaper option on a screen.

words.en: I want to withdraw one hundred euros.
words.note: States the amount for the transaction.

words.es: Pido el recibo con la comisión visible.
words.en: I ask for the receipt with the fee visible.
words.note: Requests proof that shows each charge.

words.es: El cajero se lo imprime al final.
words.en: The ATM will print it for you at the end.
words.note: Se lo: le becomes se before lo. Lo is the receipt.

example.target: Retiro cien euros del cajero.
example.native: I withdraw one hundred euros from the ATM.

verbs.note: Retirar is regular and takes the money as its direct object.

example.target: Elijo la moneda local.
example.native: I choose the local currency.

verbs.note: Elegir changes e to i in most forms; the first person is elijo.

example.target: El banco cobra tres euros por retiro.
example.native: The bank charges three euros per withdrawal.

verbs.note: Cobrar with por names the reason for a charge.

example.target: Imprimo el recibo para usted.
example.native: I print the receipt for you.

verbs.note: Imprimir is regular: imprimo, imprime. The past participle is impreso or imprimido.

passage.title: Pagar con tarjeta en otra moneda
target: Inés: Buenas tardes. ¿Quién hace la conversión si pago con tarjeta?
Cajero: La terminal le pregunta si quiere pagar en euros o en dólares.
Inés: ¿Y qué tipo de cambio aplica la terminal?
Cajero: Si elige dólares, la terminal convierte y muestra su tipo en la pantalla. Si elige euros, convierte su banco.
Inés: Prefiero pagar en euros y luego reviso el cargo que aplica mi banco.
Cajero: Si duda, le recomiendo que compare el tipo de la pantalla con el de su banco.
Inés: Perfecto. Elijo euros y confirmo el pago.
Cajero: Muy bien. Son noventa y cinco euros. Acerque la tarjeta, por favor.
native: Inés: Good afternoon. Who makes the conversion if I pay by card?
Cashier: The terminal asks you whether you want to pay in euros or in dollars.
Inés: And which exchange rate does the terminal apply?
Cashier: If you choose dollars, the terminal converts and shows its rate on the screen. If you choose euros, your bank converts.
Inés: I prefer to pay in euros and then check the charge my bank applies.
Cashier: If you are unsure, I recommend that you compare the rate on the screen with your bank's.
Inés: Perfect. I choose euros and confirm the payment.
Cashier: Very well. It is ninety-five euros. Hold the card to the reader, please.

words.note: Changing an amount from one currency into another, done by the shop, the bank or the terminal.
The device that reads a card and asks for a confirmation.
A plastic payment card, such as a debit or credit card.
An amount added to a payment by a bank or service.
The institution that holds your account and issues your card.
The display that shows the amount and the currency.
The rate used to convert one currency into the other.
The type of money used for a payment.
The act of paying a price or bill.
A fixed amount charged for a service.

words.es: ¿Quién hace la conversión si pago con tarjeta?
words.en: Who makes the conversion if I pay by card?
words.note: A direct question about which party changes the currency.

words.es: ¿Qué tipo de cambio aplica la terminal?
words.en: Which exchange rate does the terminal apply?
words.note: Asks for the rate used in the card transaction.

words.en: I prefer to pay in euros.
words.note: Expresses your choice of currency with a reason implied.

words.es: Elijo euros y confirmo el pago.
words.en: I choose euros and confirm the payment.
words.note: Confirms the choice before the card is charged.

words.es: Le recomiendo que compare el tipo de la pantalla.
words.en: I recommend that you compare the rate on the screen.
words.note: Recomendar que is followed by a subjunctive: compare, not compara.

example.target: El banco aplica un cargo por conversión.
example.native: The bank applies a charge for conversion.

verbs.note: Aplicar is regular. It is used for rates, fees and discounts that are applied to a payment.

example.target: Pase la tarjeta, por favor.
example.native: Swipe the card, please.

verbs.note: Pasar la tarjeta means to swipe or present a card. Pase is the usted command.

example.target: Prefiero pagar en euros.
example.native: I prefer to pay in euros.

verbs.note: Preferir changes e to ie in most forms, and preferimos keeps the e.

example.target: Le recomiendo que compare el tipo de la pantalla.
example.native: I recommend that you compare the rate on the screen.

verbs.note: Recomendar changes e to ie, and it is followed by que plus a subjunctive form.

passage.title: Dividir el dinero para el día
target: Carmen: Quiero cambiar este billete de cincuenta por billetes más pequeños.
Empleada: Le doy dos billetes de veinte y uno de diez.
Carmen: Tengo un presupuesto de sesenta euros para hoy.
Empleada: Entonces tiene bastante dinero para un día tranquilo.
Carmen: El autobús cuesta dos euros, la entrada al museo doce y la comida quince.
Carmen: Me quedan más de treinta euros, así que puedo comprar un regalo.
Empleada: Sí. Si no gasta mucho en el regalo, todavía le sobra dinero.
Carmen: Si el regalo cuesta diez euros, me quedan veintiún euros: menos de treinta.
native: Carmen: I want to change this fifty-euro note into smaller notes.
Clerk: I will give you two twenty-euro notes and one ten-euro note.
Carmen: I have a budget of sixty euros for today.
Clerk: Then you have enough money for a calm day.
Carmen: The bus costs two euros, the museum entry twelve and lunch fifteen.
Carmen: I have more than thirty euros left, so I can buy a present.
Clerk: Yes. If you do not spend much on the gift, you still have money left over.
Carmen: If the gift costs ten euros, I have twenty-one euros left: less than thirty.

words.note: A planned amount of money for a day, trip or purchase.
A paper note of money; the plural billetes is used for several notes.
A ticket that lets you into a museum or show.
The meal eaten in the middle of the day; also the general word for food.
Something bought or given as a present.
Money in general, in notes, coins or account balances.
The part of an amount that remains after an expense is paid.
A payment made for something needed or wanted.
A public vehicle that travels along a fixed route.

words.es: Tengo un presupuesto de sesenta euros para hoy.
words.en: I have a budget of sixty euros for today.
words.note: States the planned amount for the day.

words.es: Me quedan más de treinta euros.
words.en: I have more than thirty euros left.
words.note: Describes the remaining money after several expenses.

words.es: Quiero cambiar este billete por billetes más pequeños.
words.en: I want to change this note into smaller notes.
words.note: A specific request for change with a clear purpose.

words.es: Tengo bastante dinero para un día tranquilo.
words.en: I have enough money for a calm day.
words.note: Confirms that the budget is sufficient.

words.es: Me quedan menos de treinta euros.
words.en: I have less than thirty euros left.
words.note: States an upper limit for the money that remains.

example.target: Me quedan treinta euros.
example.native: I have thirty euros left.

verbs.note: Quedar is used with me to describe what remains, and the verb agrees with the thing that remains.

example.target: Gasto dos euros en el autobús.
example.native: I spend two euros on the bus.

verbs.note: Gastar is regular and takes the money as its direct object.

example.target: Me sobra dinero para el regalo.
example.native: I have money left over for the gift.

verbs.note: Sobrar is used with me to mean there is extra, and it agrees with the amount.

passage.title: Un taxi al aeropuerto
target: Hana: Buenas noches. ¿Cuánto cuesta ir hasta el aeropuerto?
Taxista: Depende del tráfico. El taxímetro empieza con una bajada de bandera de tres euros con cincuenta.
Hana: ¿Y cobra algún suplemento por las maletas?
Taxista: Sí, dos euros por cada maleta grande.
Hana: ¿Puedo pagar con tarjeta, o solo en efectivo?
Taxista: Sí, acepto tarjeta, pero debe decírmelo antes de llegar.
Hana: Entonces lo confirmo ahora: acepto el suplemento de las maletas y pago con tarjeta.
Taxista: Perfecto. Suba, que tengo el motor encendido.
native: Hana: Good evening. How much does it cost to go to the airport?
Driver: It depends on the traffic. The meter starts with a flag-fall of three euros fifty.
Hana: And do you charge any supplement for the suitcases?
Driver: Yes, two euros for each large suitcase.
Hana: Can I pay by card, or only in cash?
Driver: Yes, I accept cards, but you must tell me before we arrive.
Hana: Then I confirm it now: I accept the suitcase supplement and I will pay by card.
Driver: Perfect. Get in, the engine is running.

words.note: The device in a taxi that shows the fare as the trip goes on.
The price charged for a trip, which may depend on distance and time.
An extra amount added to a fare, for example for luggage or night travel.
A case for clothes and personal items when you travel.
The place where planes take off and land.
The vehicles on the road, which can slow down a trip.
The starting fare shown on the meter before the trip begins.
Money in notes and coins, not a card.
A plastic payment card.

words.en: How much does it cost to go to the airport?
words.note: Asks the total for a named destination before you get in.

words.en: Do you charge any supplement for the suitcases?
words.note: Checks an extra cost before the trip starts.

words.es: ¿Puedo pagar con tarjeta, o solo en efectivo?
words.en: Can I pay by card, or only in cash?
words.note: Asks which payment method is accepted in the vehicle.

words.es: Entonces lo confirmo antes de subir.
words.en: Then I confirm it before getting in.
words.note: Settles the price in words before the trip begins.

words.es: Suba, por favor, que tengo prisa.
words.en: Get in, please, I am in a hurry.
words.note: A driver's request that starts the ride.

example.target: El taxímetro empieza con tres euros.
example.native: The meter starts with three euros.

verbs.note: Empezar changes e to ie in every form except nosotros, which keeps empezamos.

example.target: Debe decírmelo antes de llegar.
example.native: You must tell me before we arrive.

verbs.note: Deber plus an infinitive expresses obligation. With an amount it means to owe: debo diez euros.

example.target: Subo al taxi con las maletas.
example.native: I get into the taxi with the suitcases.

verbs.note: Subir means to go up or to get in a vehicle. Its usted command is suba.

example.target: El taxi llega en dos minutos.
example.native: The taxi arrives in two minutes.

verbs.note: Llegar is regular. Use it with a place and the preposition a: llegar al aeropuerto.

passage.title: La diferencia en el taxi
target: Pablo: Acordamos dieciocho euros, ¿verdad?
Taxista: Eso era antes del tráfico. Ahora son veinticuatro euros.
Pablo: El taxímetro marcaba diecinueve euros al final del trayecto, ¿no?
Taxista: Cobro los diecinueve del taxímetro más cinco de suplemento de noche.
Pablo: Ese suplemento no lo acordamos. Quiero el recibo con el desglose.
Taxista: Aquí tiene: tarifa, distancia y suplemento de noche.
Pablo: Veo la diferencia: son seis euros más de lo acordado.
Taxista: El suplemento de noche aparece en el recibo. Si no está de acuerdo, puede reclamar.
Pablo: Pago los veinticuatro, guardo el recibo y reclamo la diferencia después.
native: Pablo: We agreed on eighteen euros, right?
Driver: That was before the traffic. Now it is twenty-four euros.
Pablo: The meter showed nineteen euros at the end of the trip, didn't it?
Driver: I charge the nineteen on the meter plus five for the night supplement.
Pablo: We did not agree that supplement. I want the receipt with the breakdown.
Driver: Here it is: fare, distance and night supplement.
Pablo: I see the difference: it is six euros more than what we agreed.
Driver: The night supplement appears on the receipt. If you do not agree, you can file a claim.
Pablo: I will pay the twenty-four, keep the receipt and claim the difference later.

words.note: The device that shows the fare during the journey.
A price or condition that both parties have accepted in advance.
A written record of what was charged.
An extra cost added to the fare, such as a night charge.
The gap between the agreed amount and the requested amount.
The list that separates each charge in a bill or receipt.
The route you travel from start to end.
The sum of money requested for a service.
A formal request to correct a charge you believe is wrong.

words.en: We agreed on eighteen euros, right?
words.note: Restates the agreed price to check the other person's memory.

words.en: Do you charge a night supplement?
words.note: Asks about an extra charge before paying.

words.es: Quiero el recibo con el desglose.
words.en: I want the receipt with the breakdown.
words.note: Requests each part of the total in writing.

words.es: Son seis euros más de lo acordado.
words.en: It is six euros more than what we agreed.
words.note: Points out the exact difference in the amount.

words.es: Pago, guardo el recibo y reclamo la diferencia después.
words.en: I will pay, keep the receipt and claim the difference later.
words.note: Closes the payment with a clear plan for the disputed amount.

example.target: Acordamos dieciocho euros antes del viaje.
example.native: We agreed on eighteen euros before the trip.

verbs.note: Acordar changes o to ue, except in nosotros, which keeps acordamos.

example.target: El taxímetro marca diecinueve euros.
example.native: The meter shows nineteen euros.

verbs.note: Marcar is regular. It is used for numbers that a device displays.

example.target: Reclamo la diferencia por escrito.
example.native: I claim the difference in writing.

verbs.note: Reclamar is regular; use it when you ask for money or a correction back.

example.target: Pago lo acordado en efectivo.
example.native: I pay what was agreed in cash.

verbs.note: In lo acordado, lo is the neuter article: lo acordado means what was agreed.

passage.title: Pagar el viaje desde el teléfono
target: Sara: Buenas tardes. ¿Usted es el conductor de la aplicación?
Conductor: Sí, soy yo. Suba, por favor.
Sara: ¿El viaje ya está pagado en la aplicación?
Conductor: Sí, la aplicación ya cobró la tarifa.
Sara: ¿Todavía tengo que pagar algo en efectivo?
Conductor: No, solo la propina si quiere dejarla.
Sara: ¿Dónde se añade la propina?
Conductor: Puede darla en la aplicación. No es obligatoria.
Sara: Perfecto. Ya tengo el recibo en el teléfono.
native: Sara: Good afternoon. Are you the driver from the app?
Driver: Yes, it is me. Please get in.
Sara: Is the trip already paid in the app?
Driver: Yes, the app has already charged the fare.
Sara: Do I still have to pay anything in cash?
Driver: No, only the tip if you want to leave one.
Sara: Where is the tip added?
Driver: You can give it in the app. It is not required.
Sara: Perfect. I already have the receipt on my phone.

words.note: A program on a phone that books and pays for the ride.
The person who drives the vehicle. The feminine form is conductora.
An extra amount given to say thanks for service. It is not required in every place.
The amount charged for the journey.
A proof of the payment, in paper or on a phone.
Money in notes and coins.
A mobile device used to order rides and show receipts.
A journey from a starting place to a destination.
Describes a charge that has already been settled.

words.es: ¿El viaje ya está pagado en la aplicación?
words.en: Is the trip already paid in the app?
words.note: Checks whether the app has settled the fare.

words.es: ¿Todavía tengo que pagar algo en efectivo?
words.en: Do I still have to pay anything in cash?
words.note: Asks about any amount still owed after the app payment.

words.es: Puede dar la propina en la aplicación.
words.en: You can give the tip in the app.
words.note: Explains a tip option without requiring it.

words.es: Ya tengo el recibo en el teléfono.
words.en: I already have the receipt on my phone.
words.note: Confirms the closing point of the transaction.
A driver's request that begins the ride.

example.target: La aplicación cobra la tarifa al final.
example.native: The app charges the fare at the end.

verbs.note: Cobrar is regular. The app is the subject, and it charges the trip automatically.

example.target: Puede añadir la propina en la aplicación.
example.native: You can add the tip in the app.

verbs.note: Añadir is regular. App buttons often show the infinitive añadir or the tú command añade.

example.target: El conductor llega en dos minutos.
example.native: The driver arrives in two minutes.

verbs.note: Llegar is regular. Use it with a place and the preposition a.

example.target: Sube al coche y se pone el cinturón.
example.native: She gets into the car and puts on the seatbelt.

verbs.note: Subir is regular. Taxis and cars use subir a for getting in.

passage.title: Billetes para el metro
target: Ivo: Quisiera un billete para el metro. ¿Qué opciones ofrece?
Taquillero: Tenemos un billete sencillo, uno de diez viajes y uno de un día.
Ivo: ¿Cuántos viajes incluye el de diez?
Taquillero: Diez viajes, válidos durante un año desde la primera validación.
Ivo: ¿El precio final incluye el depósito de la tarjeta?
Taquillero: No. El billete cuesta 20,50 euros, y el depósito de la tarjeta es de 1 euro aparte.
Ivo: Entonces pago 21,50 euros en total.
Taquillero: Exacto. ¿Quiere recarga automática después?
Ivo: No, gracias. Guardo el billete hasta que se acabe.
native: Ivo: I would like a ticket for the metro. What options do you offer?
Ticket clerk: We have a single ticket, a ten-trip ticket and a one-day ticket.
Ivo: How many journeys does the ten-trip ticket include?
Ticket clerk: Ten journeys, valid for one year from the first validation.
Ivo: Does the final price include the card deposit?
Ticket clerk: No. The ticket costs 20.50 euros, and the card deposit is 1 euro extra.
Ivo: So I pay 21.50 euros in total.
Ticket clerk: Exactly. Do you want automatic top-up afterward?
Ivo: No, thank you. I will keep the ticket until it runs out.

words.note: A paper or card ticket that allows a journey or set of journeys.
One trip on the metro, bus or train.
The period in which a ticket can be used.
An amount paid in advance and returned when the card is handed back.
Adding money or journeys to a card.
The counter where tickets are sold.
An underground railway in a city.
The total to pay. Ask whether a card deposit is added on top.
A ticket for one journey.

words.en: How many journeys does the ten-trip one include?
words.note: Asks the number of journeys in a bundle.

words.es: El billete es válido durante un año.
words.en: The ticket is valid for one year.
words.note: States the period in which the ticket works.

words.es: Son 20,50 euros, y el depósito es de 1 euro.
words.en: It is 20.50 euros, and the deposit is 1 euro.
words.note: Gives the fare and the deposit separately before the total.

words.en: So I pay 21.50 euros in total.
words.note: Confirms the total that includes the deposit.

words.es: Guardo el billete hasta que se acabe.
words.en: I keep the ticket until it runs out.
words.note: Closes the purchase with a plan for using the ticket.

example.target: ¿Qué opciones ofrece la taquilla?
example.native: What options does the ticket office offer?

verbs.note: Ofrecer is irregular in the first person: ofrezco. It is used for services and options.

example.target: Guardo el billete en la cartera.
example.native: I keep the ticket in my wallet.

verbs.note: Guardar is regular; it means to keep, store or save.

example.target: Se acaba el saldo del billete.
example.native: The balance on the ticket runs out.

verbs.note: Acabar is regular. Acabarse is used when something runs out by itself.

example.target: El bono incluye diez viajes.
example.native: The bundle includes ten journeys.

verbs.note: Incluir has a y in several forms; it is used for what a ticket covers.

passage.title: Pagar la estancia en el hotel
target: Recepcionista: Buenas tardes. ¿Tiene una reserva a nombre de Cruz?
Huésped: Sí, tres noches. ¿El total incluye el desayuno?
Recepcionista: Sí, el desayuno está incluido, y el total son trescientos euros.
Huésped: ¿Se paga al llegar o al salir?
Recepcionista: Puede pagar al salir, con tarjeta o en efectivo.
Huésped: ¿Y todo está en euros, incluidos los cargos del servicio?
Recepcionista: Sí, todo está en euros. Los cargos del servicio ya están dentro del precio.
Huésped: Entonces pago al salir, y salimos el jueves.
Recepcionista: Perfecto. Le preparo la factura para el jueves.
native: Receptionist: Good afternoon. Do you have a reservation under the name Cruz?
Guest: Yes, three nights. Does the total include breakfast?
Receptionist: Yes, breakfast is included, and the total is three hundred euros.
Guest: Do you pay on arrival or on departure?
Receptionist: You can pay on departure, by card or in cash.
Guest: And is everything in euros, including the service charges?
Receptionist: Yes, everything is in euros. The service charges are already included in the price.
Guest: Then I pay on departure, and we leave on Thursday.
Receptionist: Perfect. I will prepare the bill for Thursday.

words.note: A booking made in advance for a room or a seat.
A person who stays at a hotel or is invited to a place.
The first meal of the day, sometimes included in the room rate.
The period of time you spend in a place.
The place in a hotel where guests check in and pay.
One night of a hotel stay.
The final amount for the stay.
An amount added for service or a specific item.
A document that lists what you owe for a stay or purchase.
Checks whether a meal is part of the room price.

words.es: ¿Se paga al llegar o al salir?
words.en: Do you pay on arrival or on departure?
words.note: Asks when the payment is due.

words.es: Puede pagar al salir, con tarjeta o en efectivo.
words.en: You can pay on departure, by card or in cash.
words.note: States the payment timing and methods allowed.

words.es: Todo está en euros y los cargos ya están dentro del precio.
words.en: Everything is in euros and the charges are already included in the price.
words.note: Confirms the currency and the included charges.

words.es: Le preparo la factura para el jueves.
words.en: I will prepare the bill for Thursday.
words.note: Confirms that the bill will be ready for the departure day.

example.target: Reservamos tres noches a nombre de Cruz.
example.native: We reserved three nights under the name Cruz.

verbs.note: Reservar is regular and is used for a room, a table or a seat.

example.target: Salimos el jueves por la mañana.
example.native: We leave on Thursday morning.

verbs.note: Salir is irregular in the first person: salgo. Use it for leaving a hotel or a place.

example.target: Llegamos al hotel a las seis.
example.native: We arrive at the hotel at six.

verbs.note: Llegar is regular and used for arrival at a place.

example.target: El precio incluye el desayuno.
example.native: The price includes breakfast.

verbs.note: Incluir has a y in several forms; use it for what a price covers.

passage.title: Una retención en la tarjeta
target: Mónica: Buenas noches. ¿Me cobran el depósito o solo me retienen el dinero?
Recepcionista: Solo hacemos una retención en la tarjeta. No es un cargo.
Mónica: ¿Cuándo se libera la retención?
Recepcionista: La liberamos cuando usted salga, si no hay cargos extra.
Mónica: ¿Y cuándo vuelvo a tener ese dinero disponible?
Recepcionista: Eso depende de su banco; a veces tarda varios días hábiles. No lo sabemos con exactitud.
Mónica: ¿Me da por escrito la cantidad retenida?
Recepcionista: Claro. Son doscientos euros retenidos en su tarjeta, sin cobrar.
native: Mónica: Good evening. Do you charge me the deposit, or do you only hold the money?
Receptionist: We only place a hold on the card. It is not a charge.
Mónica: When is the hold released?
Receptionist: We release it when you leave, if there are no extra charges.
Mónica: And when will that money be available to me again?
Receptionist: That depends on your bank; it sometimes takes several business days. We do not know exactly.
Mónica: Can you give me the amount held in writing?
Receptionist: Of course. It is two hundred euros held on your card, not charged.

words.note: An amount reserved on a card that is not yet charged.
A sum paid or reserved to cover possible costs or damage.
To free an amount that was held so it becomes available again.
The institution that issues your card and controls your money.
A plastic payment card used for holds and charges.
An amount actually taken from the account or card.
The sum of money being held or charged.
A room in a hotel for guests to stay in.
A hotel worker who welcomes guests and handles check-in.

words.es: ¿Me cobran el depósito o solo me retienen el dinero?
words.en: Do you charge me the deposit, or only hold the money?
words.note: Asks the key difference between a charge and a hold.
Asks when the reserved amount becomes available again.

words.es: Solo hacemos una retención en la tarjeta.
words.en: We only place a hold on the card.
words.note: States that money is reserved, not taken.

words.en: We release it when you leave.
words.note: Cuando plus subjunctive (salga) refers to a future moment.

words.es: ¿Me da por escrito la cantidad retenida?
words.en: Can you give me the amount held in writing?
words.note: Asks for written confirmation of the amount.

example.target: La liberamos al salir.
example.native: We release it when you leave.

verbs.note: Liberar is regular; it is used for money that is no longer held.

example.target: El hotel retiene doscientos euros.
example.native: The hotel holds two hundred euros.

verbs.note: Retener is irregular in the first person (retengo) and changes e to ie in the other forms.

example.target: Hacemos una retención en la tarjeta.
example.native: We place a hold on the card.

verbs.note: Hacer is irregular in the first person (hago). Use it for making a hold, a booking or a payment arrangement.

example.target: No lo sabemos con exactitud.
example.native: We do not know it exactly.

verbs.note: Saber is irregular in the first person (sé, with an accent to avoid confusion with se). Use it for knowing a fact.

passage.title: Revisar la cuenta del hotel
target: Ruth: Buenos días. Quiero revisar la cuenta antes de pagar.
Cajera: Claro. Aquí tiene el desglose de la habitación y los extras.
Ruth: Mi reserva era de tres noches, pero me cobraron cuatro.
Cajera: Aquí aparece una cuarta noche, la del día trece.
Ruth: Yo me fui el día trece por la mañana. Y no consumí nada del minibar.
Cajera: Pues aquí tiene un cargo de once euros del minibar.
Ruth: Pido una cuenta detallada con la hora de cada cargo, por favor.
Cajera: Lo reviso: la cuarta noche es un error. Le doy una factura corregida en un momento.
native: Ruth: Good morning. I want to check the bill before I pay.
Cashier: Of course. Here is the breakdown of the room and the extras.
Ruth: My reservation was for three nights, but they charged me for four.
Cashier: A fourth night appears here, the night of the thirteenth.
Ruth: I left on the morning of the thirteenth. And I did not consume anything from the minibar.
Cashier: Well, there is an eleven-euro minibar charge here.
Ruth: I would like a detailed bill with the time of each charge, please.
Cashier: I am checking it: the fourth night is an error. I will give you a corrected bill in a moment.

words.note: The list of charges for a hotel stay or a restaurant meal.
A detailed list of each charge in a bill.
A confirmed arrangement for a room or flight.
One night of a hotel stay.
A small fridge in a room with drinks and snacks charged when used.
An amount added to the bill.
A written bill that can be corrected or reissued.
Shows each item and time separately.
The hotel room you stayed in.

words.es: Mi reserva era de tres noches, pero me cobraron cuatro.
words.en: My booking was for three nights, but they charged me for four.
words.note: States the difference between the booking and the bill.

words.en: I did not consume anything from the minibar.
words.note: Denies an item clearly in the past.

words.es: Pido una cuenta detallada con la hora de cada cargo.
words.en: I would like a detailed bill with the time of each charge.
words.note: Requests a full breakdown.

words.es: Lo reviso y le doy una factura corregida.
words.en: I will check it and give you a corrected bill.
words.note: A staff reply that accepts the review.

words.es: Yo me fui el día trece.
words.note: Gives the date that proves the error.

example.target: Consumí dos bebidas en el bar.
example.native: I consumed two drinks at the bar.

verbs.note: Consumir is regular. Use the preterite consumí for a finished action in the past.

example.target: Me cobraron cuatro noches.
example.native: They charged me for four nights.

verbs.note: In the preterite, cobraron is the third-person plural form for an unnamed group of staff or systems.

example.target: Reviso la cuenta antes de pagar.
example.native: I check the bill before paying.

verbs.note: Revisar is regular. Use it for careful checking.

example.target: Pido una factura detallada.
example.native: I ask for a detailed bill.

verbs.note: Pedir changes e to i in most forms; the first person is pido.

passage.title: Alquilar un coche pequeño
target: Tomás: Buenas tardes. Tengo una reserva para un coche pequeño, tres días.
Agente: Perfecto. El precio es de noventa euros, con seguro básico incluido.
Tomás: ¿El combustible está incluido o tengo que devolver el coche lleno?
Agente: No está incluido. Lo recibe lleno y hay que devolverlo lleno.
Tomás: ¿Y qué depósito retiene la empresa?
Agente: Una retención de doscientos euros en tarjeta de crédito, que se libera al devolver el coche.
Tomás: ¿Puedo usar una tarjeta de débito?
Agente: No, para el depósito hay que usar una tarjeta de crédito.
Tomás: Entonces firmo el contrato. ¿Me da una copia, por favor?
native: Tomás: Good afternoon. I have a booking for a small car, three days.
Agent: Perfect. The price is ninety euros, with basic insurance included.
Tomás: Is fuel included, or do I have to return the car full?
Agent: It is not included. You receive it full and it must be returned full.
Tomás: And what deposit does the company hold?
Agent: A hold of two hundred euros on a credit card, which is released when you return the car.
Tomás: Can I use a debit card?
Agent: No, for the deposit a credit card must be used.
Tomás: Then I will sign the contract. Can you give me a copy, please?

words.note: The hire of a car or another item for a set time.
A road vehicle for carrying passengers.
Security for the rental, often a card hold released at the end. In Spain depósito also means fuel tank.
Cover against damage or loss, sold as an extra or included in the quote.
The petrol or diesel used by the car.
The written agreement that sets the rental terms.
A card that allows payment on credit; some deposits require it.
A staff member who handles the rental counter.
The amount quoted for the rental period.

words.es: ¿El combustible está incluido o tengo que devolver el coche lleno?
words.en: Is fuel included, or do I have to return the car full?
words.note: Compares two fuel terms before you sign.

words.es: El seguro básico está incluido en el precio.
words.en: The basic insurance is included in the price.
words.note: States which cover is already part of the quote.
States a condition of the rental.

words.en: Can I use a debit card?
words.note: Asks whether your card is accepted for the deposit.

words.es: ¿Me da una copia del contrato, por favor?
words.en: Can you give me a copy of the contract, please?
words.note: Requests written proof of the agreement.

example.target: Alquilo un coche pequeño por tres días.
example.native: I rent a small car for three days.

verbs.note: Alquilar is regular. Use it when you hire a car or room for a period.

example.target: Devuelvo el coche lleno y recupero la retención.
example.native: I return the car full and get the hold released.

verbs.note: Devolver changes o to ue. Use it for giving back the car or money.

example.target: La empresa retiene el depósito en la tarjeta.
example.native: The company holds the deposit on the card.

verbs.note: Retener is irregular in the first person (retengo); it is used for an amount that is held, not charged.

example.target: Firmo el contrato después de revisarlo.
example.native: I sign the contract after checking it.

verbs.note: Firmar is regular. Use it before a rental starts.

passage.title: El combustible en la devolución
target: Giulia: Buenos días. Cuando devolví el coche ayer, el depósito estaba lleno.
Agente: Según el recibo, hay un cargo de combustible de cuarenta euros.
Giulia: Eso no es correcto. Las condiciones decían que había que devolver el coche lleno, y lo hice.
Agente: Revisamos el nivel registrado al devolverlo.
Giulia: Por favor, muéstreme la lectura del medidor en el momento de la entrega.
Agente: Aquí el registro marca el depósito lleno a las nueve y diez.
Giulia: Entonces debe quitar el cargo, porque el coche estaba lleno cuando lo devolví.
Agente: Tiene razón, el cargo es un error. Le doy un recibo corregido en un momento.
native: Giulia: Good morning. When I returned the car yesterday, the tank was full.
Agent: According to the receipt, there is a fuel charge of forty euros.
Giulia: That is not correct. The terms said the car had to be returned full, and I did that.
Agent: We check the level recorded at the return.
Giulia: Please show me the reading of the gauge at the moment of the return.
Agent: Here the record shows the tank full at ten past nine.
Giulia: Then you must remove the charge, because the car was full when I returned it.
Agent: You are right, the charge is an error. I will give you a corrected receipt in a moment.

words.note: The petrol or diesel that the car uses.
The amount of fuel left in the tank.
The container that holds the fuel; also a deposit in another context.
The number or level shown on a gauge or meter.
An amount added to the rental bill.
The rules of the rental that both parties must follow.
A printed or digital proof of the return and the charges.
The act of bringing back a rented car.
A dial or screen that shows the fuel level.

words.es: Cuando devolví el coche, el depósito estaba lleno.
words.en: When I returned the car, the tank was full.
words.note: States the condition at the moment of return.

words.es: Las condiciones decían que había que devolver el coche lleno.
words.en: The terms said the car had to be returned full.
words.note: Quotes the stated fuel requirement.

words.es: Muéstreme la lectura del medidor, por favor.
words.en: Please show me the gauge reading.
words.note: Asks for the evidence behind the fuel charge.

words.es: Debe quitar el cargo si el coche estaba lleno.
words.en: You must remove the charge if the car was full.
words.note: States the correction required.

words.es: Le doy un recibo corregido en un momento.
words.en: I will give you a corrected receipt in a moment.
words.note: A staff reply that accepts the correction.

example.target: Devuelvo el coche lleno de combustible.
example.native: I return the car full of fuel.

verbs.note: Devolver changes o to ue in the present, and devolví is the preterite form used for a completed return.

example.target: El sistema registra el nivel al devolverlo.
example.native: The system records the level when it is returned.

verbs.note: Registrar is regular; it is used for data kept by a system or a logbook.

example.target: Quito el cargo del recibo.
example.native: I remove the charge from the receipt.

verbs.note: Quitar is regular; it means to take away or to remove.

example.target: Revisamos el nivel al entregar el coche.
example.native: We check the level when the car is handed over.

verbs.note: Revisar is regular and used for an inspection before or after a rental.

passage.title: Un peaje en el aviso
target: Ricardo: Buenas tardes. Recibí un aviso de peaje y de aparcamiento.
Agente: Sí. El peaje lo cobró la empresa de autopistas y el aparcamiento lo cobró el aeropuerto, no nosotros.
Ricardo: ¿Y el cargo de gestión que aparece aparte es de ustedes?
Agente: Sí, es nuestra tarifa administrativa por tramitar el peaje.
Ricardo: Lo que cobran en total no coincide con el importe del peaje.
Agente: Es el peaje más nuestra tarifa. Puede pedir la factura de la autopista y comprobar la fecha y el importe.
Ricardo: Entonces pido el aviso por escrito, con cada cargo separado.
Agente: Se lo envío hoy mismo por correo electrónico.
native: Ricardo: Good afternoon. I received a notice for a toll and for parking.
Agent: Yes. The toll was charged by the motorway company and the parking by the airport, not by us.
Ricardo: And is the handling charge that appears separately yours?
Agent: Yes, it is our administrative fee for processing the toll.
Ricardo: What you charge in total does not match the toll amount.
Agent: It is the toll plus our fee. You can ask for the motorway invoice and check the date and the amount.
Ricardo: Then I would like the notice in writing, with each charge listed separately.
Agent: I will send it to you by email today.

words.note: A fee paid to use a road or motorway.
A place to leave a car, often charged by time.
A written message that informs you of a charge or problem.
A fee for processing a payment or a notice.
A road for fast traffic that often has tolls.
The work done to process a payment or document.
The sum shown on a notice or invoice.
A document listing each item or service charged.
Short for correo electrónico here; correo can also mean the postal service.

words.es: El peaje lo cobró la empresa de autopistas.
words.en: The toll was collected by the motorway company.
words.note: Identifies the provider that charged the fee.

words.es: ¿El cargo de gestión es aparte del peaje?
words.en: Is the handling charge separate from the toll?
words.note: Checks whether an administrative charge is a separate line.

words.es: Lo que cobran en total no coincide con el peaje.
words.en: What you charge in total does not match the toll.
words.note: Describes the mismatch in a precise way.

words.es: Pido el aviso por escrito, con cada cargo separado.
words.en: I would like the notice in writing, with each charge listed separately.
words.note: Requests an itemized document.

words.es: Se lo envío hoy mismo por correo electrónico.
words.en: I will send it to you by email today.
words.note: A staff reply that states the method and timing.

example.target: La empresa cobra una tarifa por el trámite.
example.native: The company charges a fee for the procedure.

verbs.note: The amount is the direct object and the payer is indirect: le cobran diez euros. Por names the reason: por el trámite.

example.target: Tramitamos el aviso en dos días.
example.native: We process the notice in two days.

verbs.note: Tramitar is regular. It is used for administrative work such as a claim or a payment request.

example.target: Los dos importes coinciden exactamente.
example.native: The two amounts match exactly.

verbs.note: Coincidir is regular; it is used to show that two details agree.

example.target: Le envío el aviso por correo electrónico.
example.native: I send you the notice by email.

verbs.note: Enviar stresses the i in singular forms and ellos: envío, envías, envía, envían. Enviamos has no written accent.

passage.title: La cuenta en el restaurante
target: Mireia: Disculpe, ¿la propina está incluida en la cuenta?
Camarero: El servicio ya está incluido en el precio, pero puede dejar algo extra.
Mireia: ¿Cuál es el total? Hay dos platos de pescado y una botella de agua.
Camarero: Son treinta y cuatro euros con cincuenta céntimos.
Mireia: Entonces pago con tarjeta y dejo cinco euros de propina.
Camarero: Perfecto. Traigo el datáfono.
Mireia: Gracias. ¿Me puede traer el recibo cuando termine?
Camarero: Claro, enseguida. Que tengan buena noche.
native: Mireia: Excuse me, is the tip included in the bill?
Waiter: The service is already included in the price, but you can leave something extra.
Mireia: What is the total? There are two fish dishes and a bottle of water.
Waiter: It is thirty-four euros and fifty cents.
Mireia: Then I pay by card and leave five euros as a tip.
Waiter: Perfect. I will bring the card machine.
Mireia: Thank you. Can you bring me the receipt when you finish?
Waiter: Of course, right away. Have a good night.

words.note: The total amount of a restaurant meal, shown on paper or on screen.
Extra money given to a waiter to thank them for service.
A service charge included in the bill or the price.
A man who serves food and drinks in a restaurant.
A portion of food served on a plate.
A device at the table that reads a card for payment.
A printed or digital proof of the payment.
The final amount after all dishes and charges.
A container of drink, such as water or wine.

words.es: ¿La propina está incluida en la cuenta?
words.en: Is the tip included in the bill?
words.note: Checks whether a tip has already been added.

words.es: El servicio ya está incluido en el precio.
words.en: The service is already included in the price.
words.note: Says the service charge is part of the total.

words.es: Son treinta y cuatro euros con cincuenta céntimos.
words.en: It is thirty-four euros and fifty cents.
words.note: States the final total with cents.

words.en: I leave five euros as a tip.
words.note: States the tip amount clearly.

words.es: ¿Me puede traer el recibo cuando termine?
words.en: Can you bring me the receipt when you finish?
words.note: Asks for proof after the card payment.

example.target: ¿Ya terminaron de comer?
example.native: Have you finished eating?

verbs.note: Terminar is regular; it is used for finishing a meal or a task.

example.target: Dejo cinco euros de propina.
example.native: I leave five euros as a tip.

verbs.note: Dejar means to leave something behind, including a tip, or to let something happen.

example.target: Traigo la cuenta en un momento.
example.native: I bring the bill in a moment.

verbs.note: Traer is irregular in the first person (traigo), used for bringing something toward the speaker.

example.target: Pago con tarjeta en la mesa.
example.native: I pay by card at the table.

verbs.note: Pagar with con names the payment method used at the table.

passage.title: Dividir la cuenta entre amigos
target: Nico: Vamos a dividir la cuenta. Cada uno paga su plato.
Lara: Bien. Pero el vino lo pagamos a medias, ¿no?
Pau: Yo no bebo vino, así que pago solo mi plato.
Nico: El vino cuesta treinta euros, así que quince cada uno. Mi plato cuesta doce, ¿y el tuyo, Lara?
Lara: Catorce. Y pido recibo por separado, para mi empresa.
Pau: Yo pago dieciséis, el precio de mi plato.
Nico: Entonces yo pago veintisiete: doce más quince.
Lara: Perfecto. Yo pago veintinueve, incluido mi plato y mi parte del vino.
Nico: Vale. Pedimos al camarero tres pagos y un recibo aparte para Lara.
native: Nico: Let us split the bill. Each person pays for their own dish.
Lara: Fine. But we split the wine equally, right?
Pau: I do not drink wine, so I pay only for my dish.
Nico: The wine costs thirty euros, so fifteen each. My dish costs twelve, and yours, Lara?
Lara: Fourteen. And I would like a separate receipt for my company.
Pau: I pay sixteen, the price of my dish.
Nico: So I pay twenty-seven: twelve plus fifteen.
Lara: Perfect. I pay twenty-nine, including my dish and my share of the wine.
Nico: Fine. We will ask the waiter for three payments and a separate receipt for Lara.

words.note: The total amount due for a shared meal.
Divided into two equal parts between people.
In separate parts or in separate receipts.
The portion of the total that one person pays.
A portion of food served to one person.
A proof of payment for each person or group.
A container for wine or water.
An alcoholic drink made from grapes, often ordered as a shared bottle.
The full amount before the split.

words.en: Each person pays for their own dish.
words.note: States the split by item.

words.en: We split the cost of the wine equally.
words.note: Proposes an equal share of a shared item.

words.es: Pido recibo por separado, para mi empresa.
words.en: I would like a separate receipt for my company.
words.note: Asks for individual proof of payment.

words.es: Yo pago dieciséis, el precio de mi plato.
words.en: I pay sixteen, the price of my dish.
words.note: States one person's share and what it covers.

words.es: Entonces, cada uno paga su parte.
words.en: So each person pays their own share.
words.note: Summarizes the agreed split.

example.target: Dividimos la cuenta entre los tres.
example.native: We divide the bill among the three of us.

verbs.note: Dividir is regular; it is used for splitting a total into parts.

example.target: Yo pago mi parte del vino.
example.native: I pay my share of the wine.

verbs.note: Pagar takes a direct object for what is paid for. Use a medias or por separado to say how.

example.target: Pido un recibo separado.
example.native: I ask for a separate receipt.

verbs.note: Pedir changes e to i in most forms. Use it for asking staff for a receipt or a dish.

example.target: Compartimos el postre entre los tres.
example.native: We share the dessert among the three of us.

verbs.note: Compartir is regular; it is used when something is split or used together.

passage.title: Regatear en el puesto de tomates
target: Ula: Buenos días. ¿Cuánto cuesta el kilo de tomates?
Vendedor: Dos euros con cincuenta el kilo. Hoy están muy buenos.
Ula: ¿Me hace un precio si compro tres kilos?
Vendedor: Si son tres kilos, le hago dos euros con veinte por kilo.
Ula: ¿Ese precio es por kilo o en total?
Vendedor: Por kilo. El total de los tres kilos es seis euros con sesenta.
Ula: Lo pienso un momento. Quiero revisar la calidad antes de decidir.
Ula: Me llevo dos kilos, entonces. ¿Me los deja también a dos euros con veinte?
Vendedor: Vale, se los dejo. Son cuatro euros con cuarenta céntimos.
native: Ula: Good morning. How much is a kilo of tomatoes?
Vendor: Two euros fifty a kilo. They are very good today.
Ula: Can you give me a better price if I buy three kilos?
Vendor: If it is three kilos, I will make it two euros twenty per kilo for you.
Ula: Is that price per kilo or in total?
Vendor: Per kilo. The total for the three kilos is six euros sixty.
Ula: I will think about it for a moment. I want to check the quality before I decide.
Ula: Then I will take two kilos. Will you let me have them at two euros twenty as well?
Vendor: All right, I will. That is four euros and forty cents.

words.note: A unit of weight used at markets; kilo is short for kilogramo.
A red fruit often sold by weight at a stall.
The amount asked for a product; regatear means to bargain for it.
A person who sells goods at a stall.
How good the product is, which you can check before buying.
The whole amount for all the items together.
A small place in a market where goods are sold.
The time of year when a product is at its best or cheapest.
The smaller unit of the euro.

words.es: ¿Me hace un precio si compro tres kilos?
words.en: Can you give me a better price if I buy three kilos?
words.note: Asks for a lower price linked to a larger quantity.

words.es: ¿Ese precio es por kilo o en total?
words.en: Is that price per kilo or in total?
words.note: Clears up the unit before you agree.

words.es: Lo pienso un momento antes de decidir.
words.en: I will think about it for a moment before I decide.
words.note: Gives time without refusing the offer.

words.en: Then I will take two kilos.
words.note: Confirms the quantity you have chosen.
Checks the total before paying.

example.target: Le hago un precio especial por tres kilos.
example.native: I make you a special price for three kilos.

verbs.note: Hacer is irregular in the first person (hago); hacer un precio means to offer a reduced price.

example.target: Lo pienso un momento.
example.native: I think about it for a moment.

verbs.note: Pensar changes e to ie. Pensar en means to think about something.

example.target: Regateo el precio en el mercado.
example.native: I bargain over the price at the market.

verbs.note: Regatear is regular and used at open-air markets where prices are negotiated.

example.target: Me llevo dos kilos.
example.native: I will take two kilos.

verbs.note: In a shop, llevarse means to take the item you have chosen.

passage.title: Precio con tarjeta y en efectivo
target: Kenji: ¿Por qué el precio con tarjeta es más alto que en efectivo?
Dependiente: Porque en efectivo le hacemos un descuento de tres euros; no es un recargo.
Kenji: Entonces el precio en efectivo es más barato que con tarjeta.
Dependiente: Sí, son cuarenta y dos euros en efectivo y cuarenta y cinco con tarjeta.
Kenji: ¿Me confirma el precio final antes de pagar?
Dependiente: Claro. Con tarjeta son cuarenta y cinco euros, sin ningún recargo añadido.
Kenji: Prefiero pagar en efectivo y ahorrar tres euros.
Dependiente: Muy bien. Aquí tiene su cambio.
native: Kenji: Why is the card price higher than the cash price?
Shop assistant: Because we give you a three-euro discount for cash; it is not a surcharge.
Kenji: So the cash price is cheaper than the card price.
Shop assistant: Yes, it is forty-two euros in cash and forty-five by card.
Kenji: Can you confirm the final price before I pay?
Shop assistant: Of course. By card it is forty-five euros, with no surcharge added.
Kenji: I prefer to pay in cash and save three euros.
Shop assistant: Very well. Here is your change.

words.note: An extra amount added to the regular price. A cash discount reduces the regular price; ask for the final total.
The amount asked for an item.
Money in notes and coins.
A plastic payment card.
A piece of clothing worn over other clothes.
A worker who serves customers in a shop. The feminine form is dependienta.
The gap between two prices.
To keep money by paying less than expected.
The price after every charge and surcharge is included.

words.es: ¿Por qué el precio con tarjeta es más alto?
words.en: Why is the price with a card higher?
words.note: Asks the reason for two different prices.

words.es: Porque en efectivo le hacemos un descuento de tres euros.
words.en: Because we give you a three-euro discount for cash.
words.note: Porque introduces the answer; por qué asks the question.

words.es: ¿Me confirma el precio final antes de pagar?
words.en: Can you confirm the final price before I pay?
words.note: Asks for confirmation before choosing the method.

words.es: Prefiero pagar en efectivo y ahorrar tres euros.
words.en: I prefer to pay in cash and save three euros.
words.note: States the payment choice and the saving.

words.es: Con tarjeta son cuarenta y cinco euros.
words.en: By card it is forty-five euros.
words.note: Gives the card total for comparison.

example.target: Ahorro tres euros si pago en efectivo.
example.native: I save three euros if I pay in cash.

verbs.note: Ahorrar is regular; use it for money you do not spend.

example.target: El pago en efectivo tiene un descuento.
example.native: The cash payment has a discount.

verbs.note: Tener is irregular: tengo, tiene. It is used here for a price feature.

example.target: Pregunto por qué cambia el precio.
example.native: I ask why the price changes.

verbs.note: Preguntar is regular and takes a por qué clause or a direct question.

example.target: Confirmo el precio final con la dependienta.
example.native: I confirm the final price with the shop assistant.

verbs.note: Confirmar is regular and used before paying.

passage.title: Señal y saldo de un apartamento
target: Lorena: Quiero confirmar la reserva del apartamento. ¿Cuánto es el depósito?
Recepción: El depósito es de 80 euros y el saldo es de 240 euros.
Lorena: ¿Cuándo tengo que pagar el saldo?
Recepción: El saldo se paga antes del 10 de diciembre, por transferencia o con tarjeta.
Lorena: ¿Hasta qué fecha puedo cancelar por escrito?
Recepción: Puede cancelar hasta el 1 de diciembre y el depósito se devuelve.
Lorena: Pago el depósito hoy, pero las condiciones las quiero por escrito, por favor.
Recepción: Le envío el documento con las condiciones por correo.
native: Lorena: I want to confirm the apartment booking. How much is the deposit?
Reception: The deposit is 80 euros and the balance is 240 euros.
Lorena: When do I have to pay the balance?
Reception: The balance is paid before 10 December, by transfer or by card.
Lorena: Until what date can I cancel in writing?
Reception: You can cancel until 1 December and the deposit is returned.
Lorena: I will pay the deposit today, but I want the terms in writing, please.
Reception: I will send you the document with the conditions by email.

words.note: An amount paid in advance to secure a booking. In Spain a booking deposit is also called la señal.
The remaining amount still to be paid after the deposit.
A confirmed arrangement for accommodation.
The act of ending a booking before the stay.
The last date by which something must be done.
The written terms that set what is allowed.
Sending money from one account to another.
A written paper or file that records terms or payments.
A self-contained flat for holiday stays.

words.en: When do I have to pay the balance?
words.note: Asks the due date for the remaining amount.

words.es: Puede cancelar hasta el 1 de diciembre.
words.note: States the last date for cancellation.

words.es: Lo quiero por escrito, por favor.
words.en: I want it in writing, please.
words.note: Asks for the terms as a written document.

words.es: Le envío el documento con las condiciones por correo.
words.en: I will send you the document with the conditions by email.
words.note: A staff reply that confirms the written terms.

example.target: Puede cancelar hasta el 1 de diciembre.
example.native: You can cancel until 1 December.

verbs.note: Cancelar is regular and used for ending a booking before a deadline.

example.target: Pago el depósito hoy.
example.native: I pay the deposit today.

verbs.note: Pagar takes the amount as its direct object.

example.target: Transfiero el saldo el lunes.
example.native: I transfer the balance on Monday.

verbs.note: Transferir changes e to ie in most forms, and transferimos keeps the e.

example.target: Recupero el depósito si cancelo a tiempo.
example.native: I get the deposit back if I cancel in time.

verbs.note: Recuperar is regular and used for money or a thing that returns to you.

passage.title: Devolver el dinero de una excursión
target: Marina: Buenas tardes. Pagué una excursión por cien euros y la cancelé.
Agente: Depende de las condiciones que firmó. ¿Me dice el número de reserva?
Marina: Sí, es el cuatro cinco dos. Cancelé con nueve días de antelación.
Agente: Según la política, se devuelve el 80 por ciento si cancela con siete días o más.
Marina: Cancelé con nueve días, así que me devuelven 80 euros, ¿verdad?
Agente: Exacto, 80 euros. Se lo devolveremos en cinco días hábiles.
Marina: ¿Cómo se devuelve el dinero, a la tarjeta o en efectivo?
Agente: A la misma tarjeta que usó para pagar.
Marina: Perfecto. Lo quiero confirmar por correo.
native: Marina: Good afternoon. I paid one hundred euros for a day tour and I cancelled it.
Agent: It depends on the terms you signed. Can you tell me the booking number?
Marina: Yes, it is four five two. I cancelled nine days in advance.
Agent: According to the policy, 80 percent is returned if you cancel seven days or more ahead.
Marina: I cancelled nine days ahead, so you return 80 euros to me, right?
Agent: Exactly, 80 euros. We will return it to you in five business days.
Marina: How is the money returned, to the card or in cash?
Agent: To the same card you used to pay.
Marina: Perfect. I want to confirm it by email.

words.note: Money returned to the payer after a cancellation or change.
The act of giving money back.
The written rules a company applies to cancellations and payments.
How early you cancel before the start of a service.
A company that books tours, flights and holidays.
A trip that you take for a day, often with a guide.
A confirmed arrangement for a tour, room or flight.
The rules that you agree to when you book.
Electronic mail used to confirm a refund.

words.en: Do they return the money if I cancel?
words.note: Asks if a refund is due.
Asks the method of refund.

words.es: Se devuelve el 80 por ciento si cancela con siete días.
words.en: 80 percent is returned if you cancel seven days ahead.
words.note: Explains the percentage and the timing rule.

words.es: Se lo devolveremos en cinco días hábiles.
words.en: We will return it to you in five business days.
words.note: States the timing promised by the agency.

words.en: I want to confirm it by email.
words.note: Asks for written confirmation of the refund.

example.target: Cancelé la excursión con antelación.
example.native: I cancelled the tour in advance.

verbs.note: Cancelar is regular; the preterite cancelé is used for a completed cancellation.

example.target: Usé la misma tarjeta para pagar.
example.native: I used the same card to pay.

verbs.note: Usar is regular. The preterite usé is used for a completed action.

example.target: Devolvemos el dinero a la tarjeta.
example.native: We return the money to the card.

verbs.note: Devolver changes o to ue. Use it for money returned to a payer.

example.target: Firmé las condiciones al reservar.
example.native: I signed the terms when I booked.

verbs.note: Firmar is regular; the preterite firmé is for a completed signing.

passage.title: Tarifa flexible o básica
target: Félix: Buenos días. Quiero una habitación con una tarifa que se pueda cancelar.
Agente: La tarifa básica cuesta 90 euros por noche, y la flexible, 110 euros: 20 euros más.
Félix: ¿Y la tarifa básica no se puede cancelar?
Agente: No, la tarifa básica no admite devolución.
Félix: ¿Me envía las condiciones exactas por escrito?
Agente: Claro. Puede cancelar hasta el día antes de la llegada, sin cargo.
Félix: Quiero la tarifa flexible, entonces.
Agente: Perfecto. Le envío la confirmación con esas condiciones.
native: Félix: Good morning. I want a room with a rate that can be cancelled.
Agent: The basic rate costs 90 euros per night, and the flexible one 110 euros: 20 euros more.
Félix: And the basic rate cannot be cancelled?
Agent: No, the basic rate does not allow a refund.
Félix: Can you send me the exact terms in writing?
Agent: Of course. You can cancel until the day before arrival, without a charge.
Félix: Then I want the flexible rate.
Agent: Perfect. I will send you the confirmation with those terms.

words.note: A rate that allows changes or cancellations, usually for a higher price.
A lower rate that often does not allow a refund.
Money returned after a cancellation.
The rules of the booking written in the confirmation.
A confirmed arrangement for a room or a flight.
The day or time when a guest or traveler arrives.
An amount charged to a card or account.
One night of a room stay.
A written proof that the booking is confirmed.

words.es: Quiero una tarifa que se pueda cancelar.
words.en: I want a rate that can be cancelled.
words.note: States the requirement clearly.

words.es: ¿La tarifa básica no se puede cancelar?
words.en: The basic rate cannot be cancelled?
words.note: Checks the cancellation rule of the cheaper option.

words.es: ¿Me envía las condiciones exactas por escrito?
words.en: Can you send me the exact terms in writing?
words.note: Requests the written terms before choosing.

words.es: Puede cancelar hasta el día antes de la llegada.
words.en: You can cancel until the day before arrival.
words.note: States the deadline for cancelling without a charge.

words.en: Then I want the flexible rate.
words.note: Makes the decision after comparing both options.

example.target: Puede cancelar hasta el día antes de la llegada.
example.native: You can cancel until the day before arrival.

verbs.note: Poder changes o to ue, and the subjunctive form pueda appears after que.

example.target: La tarifa básica no admite devolución.
example.native: The basic rate does not allow a refund.

verbs.note: Admitir is regular; it means to allow or accept a term.

example.target: Le envío las condiciones por escrito.
example.native: I send you the terms in writing.

verbs.note: Enviar stresses the i in singular forms and ellos: envío, envías, envía, envían. Enviamos has no written accent.

example.target: Se cobra la primera noche si cancela.
example.native: The first night is charged if you cancel.

verbs.note: Cobrar with se is a common passive for an unnamed charge.

passage.title: Cambiar la fecha de un viaje
target: Irene: Quiero cambiar la fecha de mi reserva. ¿Cuánto cobran por el cambio?
Agente: El cargo por cambio es de 25 euros por la operación.
Irene: Si cambiara la fecha, ¿cuánto pagaría en total?
Agente: La diferencia de precio es de 60 euros, más el cargo. Son 85 euros en total.
Irene: ¿Me queda algún crédito de la reserva anterior?
Agente: Sí, le quedan 15 euros de crédito para usar.
Irene: Entonces, con el crédito, pagaría 70 euros.
Agente: Exacto. Puedo hacer el cambio ahora mismo.
Irene: Perfecto. Hágalo, por favor.
native: Irene: I want to change the date of my booking. How much do you charge for the change?
Agent: The change fee is 25 euros for the transaction.
Irene: If I changed the date, how much would I pay in total?
Agent: The price difference is 60 euros, plus the fee. It is 85 euros in total.
Irene: Is there any credit left from the previous booking?
Agent: Yes, you have 15 euros of credit left to use.
Irene: So, with the credit, I would pay 70 euros.
Agent: Exactly. I can make the change right now.
Irene: Perfect. Please do it.

words.note: A fee for altering a booking. Avoid tasa de cambio here: in much of Latin America it means exchange rate.
An amount kept from an earlier booking that can be used later.
The extra amount between the old and the new booking.
The booking that is being changed.
The day of travel or stay.
The full amount to be paid after the fee and credit.
Altering a booking, or the money given back in a shop.
A single action that is charged.
The amount asked for the trip.

words.es: Si cambiara la fecha, ¿cuánto pagaría en total?
words.en: If I changed the date, how much would I pay in total?
words.note: Asks the total for a hypothetical change.

words.es: ¿Me queda algún crédito de la reserva anterior?
words.en: Is there any credit left from the previous booking?
words.note: Asks whether an old amount can be used.

words.es: Son 85 euros en total, con el cargo incluido.
words.en: It is 85 euros in total, with the fee included.
words.note: States the full sum including the change fee.

words.es: Entonces, con el crédito, pagaría 70 euros.
words.en: So, with the credit, I would pay 70 euros.
words.note: Calculates the net amount with the credit.
A polite instruction to proceed with the change.

example.target: Quiero cambiar la fecha de mi reserva.
example.native: I want to change the date of my booking.

verbs.note: Cambiar is regular; use it for altering a booking or exchanging money.

example.target: Me quedan 15 euros de crédito.
example.native: I have 15 euros of credit left.

verbs.note: Quedar is used with me to say what remains after a change.

example.target: Si cambio la fecha hoy, pago 70 euros con el crédito.
example.native: If I change the date today, I pay 70 euros with the credit.

verbs.note: Pago is a real present payment; the conditional pagaría describes a payment that depends on a hypothetical condition.

example.target: Uso el crédito para pagar la diferencia.
example.native: I use the credit to pay the difference.

verbs.note: Usar is regular; it is used for applying a credit or a voucher.

passage.title: Entradas a la torre
target: Nora: Buenas tardes. ¿Cuánto cuesta la entrada general a la torre?
Taquillero: Catorce euros. La visita guiada cuesta 9 euros aparte.
Nora: ¿La visita guiada está incluida en la entrada?
Taquillero: No. Tiene que pagarla aparte, en la taquilla de la planta baja, al empezar la visita.
Nora: Entonces aquí pago solo la entrada, y la visita, abajo. ¿El total es 23 euros?
Taquillero: Exacto: catorce ahora y nueve abajo, veintitrés en total. Aquí tiene su entrada.
Nora: Gracias. ¿A qué hora empieza la visita guiada?
Taquillero: Empieza a las cinco, junto a la escalera.
native: Nora: Good afternoon. How much is the general entry to the tower?
Ticket clerk: Fourteen euros. The guided visit costs 9 euros separately.
Nora: Is the guided visit included in the entry?
Ticket clerk: No. You must pay for it separately, at the ticket counter on the ground floor, when the visit starts.
Nora: So here I pay only for the entry, and for the visit downstairs. Is the total 23 euros?
Ticket clerk: Exactly: fourteen now and nine downstairs, twenty-three in total. Here is your ticket.
Nora: Thank you. What time does the guided visit start?
Ticket clerk: It starts at five, next to the stairs.

words.note: The standard ticket that gives access without a guide.
A tour led by a guide who explains the place.
The counter where tickets are sold and paid.
A tall building or structure that visitors can climb.
The level at street height, where the entrance usually is.
Not included in the price; paid as its own item.
Part of the price already counted in the total.
The sum of all tickets and options chosen.

words.es: ¿La visita guiada está incluida en la entrada?
words.en: Is the guided visit included in the entry?
words.note: Checks whether a second item is part of the first price.

words.es: Tiene que pagarla aparte, en la taquilla.
words.en: You must pay for it separately, at the counter.
words.note: States the required separate payment and where to make it.
Confirms the sum before paying.
A staff phrase when handing over a ticket.

example.target: La visita empieza a las cinco.
example.native: The visit starts at five.

verbs.note: Empezar changes e to ie except in nosotros, which keeps empezamos.

example.target: Pago la entrada en la taquilla.
example.native: I pay for the entry at the ticket counter.

verbs.note: Pagar takes the item paid for as its object; the object pronoun can attach to the infinitive.

example.target: La entrada incluye el mapa.
example.native: The entry includes the map.

verbs.note: Incluir has a y in several forms; it names what a price covers.

passage.title: Lavar la ropa de viaje
target: Omar: Buenos días. ¿Cómo cobran el lavado de la ropa?
Encargada: Depende. Cobramos por kilo o por prenda, según lo que traiga.
Omar: Tengo tres camisas y un pantalón. ¿Cuánto sería por prenda?
Encargada: Cada prenda cuesta cuatro euros, sin planchar.
Omar: ¿Y por kilo? Creo que pesan unos tres kilos.
Encargada: Por kilo son dos euros con cincuenta; tres kilos, siete euros con cincuenta, con secado.
Omar: Por prenda serían dieciséis euros, así que por kilo me conviene más. ¿La tienen para mañana?
Encargada: Sí, la tendremos lista mañana al mediodía. Pagará al recogerla.
native: Omar: Good morning. How do you charge for washing clothes?
Manager: It depends. We charge by the kilo or by the item, depending on what you bring.
Omar: I have three shirts and one pair of trousers. How much would it be per item?
Manager: Each item costs four euros, without ironing.
Omar: And by the kilo? I think they weigh about three kilos.
Manager: By the kilo it is two euros fifty; three kilos, seven euros fifty, with drying.
Omar: Per item it would be sixteen euros, so by the kilo suits me better. Will it be ready for tomorrow?
Manager: Yes, it will be ready tomorrow at midday. You will pay when you collect it.

words.note: A shop or service that washes clothes for customers.
One piece of clothing counted separately in a price.
A unit of weight used to price laundry by weight.
The step that dries clothes, sometimes included in the price.
Pressing clothes with an iron; sometimes charged as a separate service.
Garments collected for washing.
A garment with buttons worn on the upper body.
A garment covering the legs, counted as one item.
The time around twelve o'clock when a pick-up is often set.

words.es: ¿Cómo cobran el lavado de la ropa?
words.en: How do you charge for washing clothes?
words.note: Asks how the service is priced before you commit.

words.en: How much would it be per item?
words.note: Asks the price for one item unit.

words.es: Por kilo son dos euros con cincuenta.
words.en: By the kilo it is two euros fifty.
words.note: States the price by weight.

words.es: Entonces por kilo me conviene más.
