words.en: Then by the kilo suits me better.
words.note: Chooses the cheaper unit for your load.

words.en: You will pay when you collect it.
words.note: States the payment time for the laundry.

example.target: El precio depende del peso.
example.native: The price depends on the weight.

verbs.note: Depender is regular; it is followed by de for what the price relies on.

example.target: No plancho la ropa, solo la lavo.
example.native: I do not iron the clothes, I only wash them.

verbs.note: Planchar is regular and often sold as a separate service.

example.target: Recojo la ropa mañana al mediodía.
example.native: I collect the clothes tomorrow at midday.

verbs.note: Recoger is irregular in the first person (recojo). It is used for collecting an item from a shop.

example.target: Lavo las camisas a mano.
example.native: I wash the shirts by hand.

verbs.note: Lavar is regular and takes the clothes as its object.

passage.title: Enviar dinero a un familiar
target: Leo: Quiero enviar 300 euros a mi hermana. ¿Cuánto recibirá en su moneda?
Agente: La comisión de 12 euros se descuenta de los 300, así que se convierten 288 euros.
Leo: ¿Y a qué tipo de cambio?
Agente: Hoy aplicamos 1,10 dólares por euro, así que recibirá 316,80 dólares.
Leo: ¿Cuándo estará disponible el dinero para ella?
Agente: Llegará en unas dos horas, si el banco receptor procesa el pago hoy.
Leo: Confirme el nombre del destinatario, por favor.
Agente: Destinataria: Lucía Ramos, con cuenta en un banco local.
Leo: Perfecto. Deme el comprobante de la transferencia; lo guardo yo.
native: Leo: I want to send 300 euros to my sister. How much will she receive in her currency?
Agent: The 12-euro fee is deducted from the 300, so 288 euros are converted.
Leo: And at what exchange rate?
Agent: Today we apply 1.10 dollars per euro, so she will receive 316.80 dollars.
Leo: When will the money be available to her?
Agent: It will arrive in about two hours, if the receiving bank processes the payment today.
Leo: Please confirm the recipient's name.
Agent: Recipient: Lucía Ramos, with an account at a local bank.
Leo: Perfect. Give me the transfer receipt; I will keep it.

words.note: The person who receives the money sent.
Sending money from one account or service to another.
The amount charged for sending the transfer.
The sum of money being sent or paid.
The type of money in which the recipient is paid.
Ready to use or collect at a given time.
A proof that the transfer was made.
The rate used to convert the amount into the other currency.
The bank where the recipient's account is held.

words.en: How much will she receive in her currency?
words.note: Asks the payout in the local currency.

words.es: ¿Cuándo estará disponible el dinero para ella?
words.en: When will the money be available for her?
words.note: Asks for the expected timing.

words.es: La comisión se descuenta de los 300 euros.
words.en: The fee is deducted from the 300 euros.
words.note: The fee comes out of the amount sent, so less is converted.

words.es: Confirme el nombre del destinatario, por favor.
words.note: Checks the person receiving the money.

words.es: Guardo el comprobante de la transferencia.
words.note: States that you keep the proof of the transfer.

example.target: Envío dinero a mi hermana cada mes.
example.native: I send money to my sister every month.

verbs.note: Enviar stresses the i in singular forms and ellos: envío, envías, envía, envían. Enviamos has no written accent.

example.target: La comisión se descuenta del importe.
example.native: The fee is deducted from the amount.

verbs.note: Descontar changes o to ue except in nosotros, which keeps descontamos.

example.target: El tipo de cambio se mantiene hoy.
example.native: The exchange rate holds today.

verbs.note: Mantener is irregular in the first person (mantengo) and changes e to ie.

example.target: Guardo el comprobante de la transferencia.
example.native: I keep the transfer receipt.

verbs.note: Guardar is regular; it means to keep a record or a document.

passage.title: El registro del día
target: Clara: Voy a anotar los gastos de hoy.
Jonás: ¿Qué has pagado hasta ahora?
Clara: He pagado el tren, el almuerzo y la entrada al museo.
Jonás: ¿Cuánto has gastado en total?
Clara: He gastado 48 euros y me quedan 102 euros.
Jonás: ¿Queda algo pendiente?
Clara: Sí, el depósito del hotel aún no está pagado, son 60 euros.
Jonás: Entonces te quedan 42 euros libres.
Clara: Perfecto. Lo apunto todo en el registro del viaje.
native: Clara: I am going to write down today's expenses.
Jonás: What have you paid so far?
Clara: I have paid for the train, lunch and the museum ticket.
Jonás: How much have you spent in total?
Clara: I have spent 48 euros and I have 102 euros left.
Jonás: Is anything still pending?
Clara: Yes, the hotel deposit has not been paid yet, it is 60 euros.
Jonás: Then you have 42 euros free.
Clara: Perfect. I will write it all in the travel record.

words.note: A written list of payments and balances kept during a trip.
A payment made for something during the trip.
Not yet paid or settled.
The midday meal.
An amount paid in advance as security.
Money not yet committed to any payment.
The sum of all the expenses added together.
A ticket that gives access to a place such as a museum.
A railway vehicle used for travel between towns.

words.es: He pagado el tren y el almuerzo.
words.en: I have paid for the train and the lunch.
words.note: Records completed payments in the present perfect.

words.en: How much have you spent in total?
words.note: Asks the total spent so far.

words.es: El depósito del hotel aún no está pagado.
words.en: The hotel deposit is not yet paid.
words.note: States a pending amount clearly.
Gives the amount left after pending items.

words.es: Lo apunto todo en el registro del viaje.
words.en: I write it all in the travel record.
words.note: Closes the review with a record.

example.target: Anoto cada gasto en el registro.
example.native: I write down each expense in the record.

verbs.note: Anotar is regular; use it for writing a note or entry.

example.target: He pagado el tren.
example.native: I have paid for the train.

verbs.note: Haber is the auxiliary used in the present perfect; the form hay means there is or there are.

example.target: Hoy he gastado 48 euros.
example.native: Today I have spent 48 euros.

verbs.note: Gastar is regular; the participle gastado is used with haber for a completed spend.

example.target: Pago el depósito mañana.
example.native: I pay the deposit tomorrow.

verbs.note: Pagar takes the item paid for as its direct object; its participle is pagado.

passage.title: La tasa turística del hotel
target: Valentina: Buenas noches. Me han dicho que hay una tasa turística por alojamiento. ¿Es así?
Recepcionista: Sí, en esta ciudad española el ayuntamiento cobra una tasa por persona y por noche.
Valentina: ¿Cuánto es por noche?
Recepcionista: Son 2 euros por persona y noche, con un máximo de 7 noches.
Valentina: ¿Quién cobra esa tasa, el hotel o el ayuntamiento?
Recepcionista: La cobramos nosotros, pero la entregamos al ayuntamiento, que es quien la fija.
Valentina: Entonces la pago al salir, junto con la cuenta.
Recepcionista: Exacto. Le daré un recibo que indique la tasa por separado.
native: Valentina: Good evening. I have been told there is a tourist tax for accommodation. Is that right?
Receptionist: Yes, in this Spanish city the council charges a tax per person and per night.
Valentina: How much is it per night?
Receptionist: It is 2 euros per person per night, with a maximum of 7 nights.
Valentina: Who collects that tax, the hotel or the city council?
Receptionist: We collect it, but we pass it to the city council, which sets it.
Valentina: Then I pay it at check-out, together with the bill.
Receptionist: Exactly. I will give you a receipt that shows the tax separately.

words.note: In Spain some regions or city councils charge visitors per night; name, rate and rules vary. Amounts here are fictional.
A place to stay, such as a hotel, hostel or apartment.
The local government of a town or city.
An individual who stays at the place and is counted for the tax.
The highest number or amount allowed.
A written proof of payment for the tax and other charges.
One night of a stay.
The total amount due at check-out.
The price or amount set for a service or tax.

words.en: How much is the tax per night?
words.note: Asks the amount per night in the local area.

words.es: Se cobra por persona y por noche.
words.en: It is charged per person and per night.
words.note: Explains how the tax is calculated.
Asks which party receives the money.

words.es: La pago al salir, junto con la cuenta.
words.en: I pay it at check-out, together with the bill.
words.note: States the timing of payment.

words.es: Le daré un recibo que indique la tasa por separado.
words.en: I will give you a receipt that shows the tax separately.
words.note: A staff promise to show the tax on its own line.

example.target: Entregamos la tasa al ayuntamiento.
example.native: We hand the tax over to the city council.

verbs.note: Entregar is regular; it is used for handing over money or documents to another party.

example.target: Me dicen que hay una tasa local.
example.native: They tell me there is a tourist tax.

verbs.note: Decir is irregular: digo for yo, and e changes to i in dices, dice and dicen.

example.target: El recibo indica la tasa por separado.
example.native: The receipt shows the tax separately.

verbs.note: Indicar is regular; it means to point out or to show clearly on a document.

example.target: Se cobra una tasa por noche.
example.native: A tax is charged per night.

verbs.note: Cobrar with se is a common impersonal form for a charge made by the place.

passage.title: Un día completo de pagos
target: Mauro: Esta mañana pagué el autobús con monedas: dos euros con cuarenta céntimos.
Mauro: Al mediodía pedí el menú del día, y el camarero me trajo una cuenta detallada.
Mauro: Pagué 16 euros con tarjeta y dejé 2 euros de propina en efectivo.
Mauro: En el hotel, la recepcionista me dijo que retendrían 120 euros hasta el jueves.
Mauro: Por la noche tomé un taxi con tarifa acordada de 9 euros, pero el taxímetro marcaba 11.
Mauro: Le pedí al conductor que me explicara la diferencia, y me dijo que era un suplemento nocturno.
Mauro: Al final pagué los 11 euros, pero guardé el recibo para reclamar los 2 de diferencia.
Amiga: ¿Te quedó algo de dinero para mañana?
Mauro: Me quedan 35 euros en efectivo, así que estoy bien.
native: Mauro: This morning I paid for the bus with coins: two euros forty cents.
Mauro: At midday I ordered the menu of the day, and the waiter brought me a detailed bill.
Mauro: I paid 16 euros by card and left 2 euros in cash as a tip.
Mauro: At the hotel, the receptionist told me they would hold 120 euros until Thursday.
Mauro: At night I took a taxi with an agreed fare of 9 euros, but the meter showed 11.
Mauro: I asked the driver to explain the difference, and he said it was a night supplement.
Mauro: In the end I paid the 11 euros, but I kept the receipt to claim the 2-euro difference.
Friend: Did you have any money left for tomorrow?
Mauro: I have 35 euros in cash left, so I am fine.

words.note: Small metal pieces of money used for bus fares and small payments.
A fixed-price meal offered at midday in many restaurants.
Extra money given to say thanks for service.
To keep an amount on a card without taking it yet.
The device that shows the fare during a taxi journey.
A fare both sides accepted before the trip.
A written proof of the payment, kept to claim later.
Money in notes and coins.
To ask for money or a correction back after a payment.

words.en: I paid for the bus with coins.
words.note: Records a completed cash payment.
States the amount and method of a meal payment.

words.es: La recepcionista me dijo que retendrían 120 euros.
words.en: The receptionist told me they would hold 120 euros.
words.note: Reports a hold using the conditional tense.

words.es: Le pedí que me explicara la diferencia.
words.en: I asked them to explain the difference.
words.note: Reports a request: pedir que plus the imperfect subjunctive explicara.

words.en: I have 35 euros in cash left.
words.note: Gives the balance for tomorrow.

words.es: Guardé el recibo para reclamar la diferencia.
words.en: I kept the receipt to claim the difference.
words.note: Records the proof needed for a later claim.

example.target: Pagué el autobús con monedas.
example.native: I paid for the bus with coins.

verbs.note: Pagar is regular; the preterite pagué is used for completed payments.

example.target: Ella dice que retendrán 120 euros.
example.native: She says they will hold 120 euros.

verbs.note: Decir is irregular; dijo is the preterite third-person form.

example.target: Guardé el recibo para reclamar la diferencia.
example.native: I kept the receipt to claim the difference.

verbs.note: Guardar is regular; guardé is the preterite first-person form.

example.target: El taxímetro marcaba 11 euros.
example.native: The meter showed 11 euros.

verbs.note: Marcar is regular; the imperfect marcaba describes what the meter was showing during the trip.
